\emph{Related (batch 80).} The report \emph{Lexicographic Orders of
Well-Orderings of the Surreal Numbers}, held in this repository at
\path{Algebra/SurrealNumbers/docs/foundations-and-computation/surreal-well-orders/}
(labels \texttt{swo:}), uses only recursions of the kind covered by
\cref{found:prop:recursion}. Each of its four sources says so in its
foundational section (its Subsections 5.3, 5.4.4, 5.5.3 and 5.6.2): every
transfinite recursion in its proofs runs along the ordinals with a set value
at each stage, determined by the set of earlier values and fixed class
parameters, and the local solutions are assembled by uniqueness and elementary
comprehension; none invokes $\ETR$. An example is the recursion building
well-orders of the sets $V_\alpha$ in the proof of its Theorem~13.1
(\texttt{swo:cf:choice}), over GB without set choice. It leaves recursions with
class-valued stages to its open questions, such as Research question~27.3
(\texttt{swo:n16.3}) on iterated residual decompositions, and warns that its
set-valued justification does not carry over unchecked to non-set-like class
well-orders.

\noindent[Added 2 October 2026, batch 80: the order-theoretic case of this
remark, which uses neither the field structure nor uncountability, is proved
and used in the report
\repo{foundations-and-computation/surreal-well-orders} (batch-80 manuscripts
08, 09, 11 and 12). Its Lemma~7.2 (\lbl{swo:sw:stageeta}, its source 11's)
shows, by the birthday bound \eqref{hset:eq:cut-bound}, that for every regular
infinite $\kappa$, $\kappa=\om$ included, $\No_{<\kappa}$ fills every cut
$A<B$ with $\card{A\cup B}<\kappa$, even avoiding any prescribed set of fewer
than $\kappa$ points; it calls this property $\eta_\kappa$. Its Note~7.4
(\lbl{swo:sk:prop:cutoffeta}, its source 08's Proposition~6.1) states it for
regular $\kappa$ with $2^{<\kappa}=\kappa$ and cites this remark. Its
Proposition~12.1 (\lbl{swo:sw:permutationeta}) shows that the lexicographic
order of the well-orderings of length $\kappa$ of an $\eta_\kappa$-order of
cardinality $\kappa$ is again $\eta_\kappa$; with Lemma~7.2 this applies to
$\No_{<\kappa}$ when $2^{<\kappa}=\kappa$. No result here uses that
report.]

\noindent[Added 2 October 2026, batch 80: a class-level counterpart. The
report \repo{foundations-and-computation/surreal-well-orders} proves in its
Theorem~13.1 (\lbl{swo:cf:choice}, its source 11's) that over GB without set
choice, Global Choice holds if and only if $\No$ has a class well-order, if and
only if it has a set-like one, if and only if there is a class bijection
$\Ord\to\No$. From a class well-order of the sign sequences, the proof
well-orders every $V_\alpha$ by set-valued recursion, coding a subset of
$V_\beta$ by a sign sequence along the well-order of $V_\beta$ already built.
Its Remark~13.4 (\lbl{swo:rem:answered-choice}) compares this with the
ordinal-graph coding of \cref{hset:thm:choice} and notes that the theorem here
concerns a different statement and is unchanged. The two open problems just
named are not affected.]

\noindent[Added 2 October 2026, batch~80: answered in part for one family of
set-sized suborders of surreal numbers, at the minimal stratum $n=0$. The
surreal-well-orders report,
\nolinkurl{Algebra/SurrealNumbers/docs/foundations-and-computation/surreal-well-orders/},
merged from batch-80 manuscripts 08, 09, 11 and~12, takes $X=S_{<\theta}$ for
an infinite cardinal $\theta$, so that $\lambda=|S_{<\theta}|=2^{<\theta}$
(it writes $\mathbf{No}_{<\theta}$; the order is the sign order of
\cref{lwo:sp:sec:surreal}). Its Theorem~8.3 (label
\texttt{swo:st:thm:transition}, source~12's) proves
$\W_\lambda(S_{<\theta})\equi\B_\lambda$, which is the case $n=0$ of the
display above, except when $\theta$ is a singular strong-limit cardinal. Then
$\lambda=\theta$ and $\W_\theta(S_{<\theta})\equi\B_{\theta\cdot\theta}$, with
the ordinal product, so $\bl(\W_\theta(S_{<\theta}))=\theta\cdot\theta>\theta$
and the display fails for $n=0$. Its Example~8.5 (\texttt{swo:st:n10.5}) takes
$\theta=\beth_\omega$, a singular strong limit in ZFC alone. The question stays
open for $n>0$, for the longer strata, for cutoffs $\theta$ that are not
cardinals, for other alphabets, and for the weakest hypotheses on $X$. The same
report reprints, with pointers to the labels here and no novelty claim, its
sources' re-proofs of results that this report proves for every infinite linear
alphabet: \cref{lwo:lem:prefix-free,lwo:prop:cardinality,lwo:lem:cut-code,lwo:thm:cube-strict,lwo:lem:eventual,lwo:thm:no-long,lwo:thm:ordinal-spectrum,lwo:lem:all-small-cubes,lwo:thm:full-length,lwo:lem:extrema,lwo:thm:adjacency,lwo:thm:blocks,lwo:sp:thm:universality}.
